idiom: to cut to the heart of the matter
meaning: to get straight to the most important point of a discussion or problem
literal_translation: перейти к сути дела, минуя детали
example: The committee chair cut to the heart of the matter by asking whether the proposal was legal.
origin: Likely from the image of cutting into a fruit to reach its core; the exact origin of the phrase is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to slice a cake into equal pieces for a party
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is figurative and refers to reaching the main point of an argument, not to cutting food

wrong_meanings.meaning: to cut short a conversation because of a deadline
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes focusing on the core issue, not ending a discussion early

wrong_meanings.meaning: to remove a sensitive passage from a document
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom concerns identifying the main point, not deleting text

explanation: 'Cut to the heart of the matter' means to focus directly on the central issue of a discussion without wasting time on side details. It is often used in debate and analysis to praise a clear, focused argument.
